extracted.subtask_description: Practical, general-audience guidance on writing effective horror fiction (short and long forms), focusing on craft, theme, reader psychology, and market/context. Emphasizes what makes horror work beyond gore and offers stylistic and thematic heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heart of Every Tale
rubrics_metrics.description: Every story contains horror fundamentally. It explores fear, tragedy, and whether characters overcome them — not just gore, but existential dread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horror is defined by exploration of fear and consequences, not graphic content alone. Aim to probe terror, tragedy, and the human response; avoid assuming gore is synonymous with horror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy's Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror stems from character flaws and poor choices. 'Tragedy is born through character flaws, through bad choices, through grave missteps.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make horror grow organically from characters' traits and decisions rather than arbitrary external events. Use flawed characters whose errors produce escalating consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary Legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror has ancient roots spanning from Beowulf to Greek mythology, establishing it as core to narrative tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize horror's deep narrative traditions; use archetypal structures and motifs intentionally rather than dismissing them as clichés.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ghost Stories and Urban Legends
rubrics_metrics.description: These simple forms contain horror's essential elements: subversion, warning, and fear of unknowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study compact forms (ghost stories, urban legends) to learn how to imply menace and deliver cautionary impact with economy and suggestiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fear of Darkness
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans are biologically programmed to fear the unknown and dark. The unknowable frightens more than the known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit the psychological power of uncertainty and the unseen. Resist over-explaining; let darkness and mystery do work for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror requires obvious consequences. Understanding what can be lost makes fear effective and visceral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish concrete, meaningful stakes early so readers care about outcomes. Vague threats diminish emotional investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dread and Revulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror operates through alternating tension: dread (anticipating bad things) and revulsion (witnessing them unfold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhythm scenes between mounting dread and payoffs of revulsion; balance anticipation against payoff to maintain emotional impact without numbing the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror affects mind (intellectual puzzlement), heart (emotional terror), and gut (primal bodily response simultaneously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to engage multiple levels—intellectual intrigue, emotional stakes, and visceral reaction—to create layered and memorable horror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disgust Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror leverages our primal enjoyment of being grossed out, a fundamental and satisfying human response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use disgust intentionally as a legitimate emotional tool, but be mindful of reader tolerance and narrative purpose to avoid gratuitousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viscera Not Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective horror doesn't need graphic content; ghost stories prove horror works without blood or gore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on gore as a shortcut. Psychological and atmospheric techniques can be equally or more effective; know when restraint serves the story better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beloved Characters Making Mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension peaks when likable characters make poor decisions that endanger themselves, creating emotional investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make readers care about characters first; then put them into avoidable jeopardy so choices matter and emotional payoff is stronger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horror and Humor Connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Both stimulate the same emotional response and use similar structures: setup, question, twist — but aim differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study comedic structures (setup/question/twist) to sharpen timing and surprise in horror. Be aware both can coexist — tonal shifts can enhance rather than ruin effect if handled deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and Death Together
rubrics_metrics.description: Both taboo subjects exist in darkness. Sex represents life-affirmation against mortality, creating complex thematic resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the interplay of desire and mortality to deepen thematic stakes; treat taboo material thoughtfully rather than for cheap shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morbid Curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans possess an instinct to witness danger (slowing at accidents, watching forbidden videos), fueling horror's appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage readers' morbid curiosity ethically to draw them into scenes, but avoid exploiting it without narrative justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre's Current Struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror once dominated bookstore shelves in the '80s-'90s but has diminished; some authors relabel books to different genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of market trends and genre perception; consider positioning and marketing, but don't let market fears undermine honest storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Resurgence
rubrics_metrics.description: Dark cultural moments may reignite horror popularity as readers seek both escape and reflection of anxieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize cultural context can make certain horrors resonate more; timely themes can amplify relevance but avoid fashionable pastiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nice Horror Writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradoxically, horror authors tend to be exceptionally kind, perhaps because writing dark fiction purges inner demons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an observational note about community and craft — cultivate empathy and professionalism even while writing dark subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hope as Essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Good and evil define each other through contrast. Horror requires hope's presence to make darkness meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include elements of hope or resistance so darkness has weight; absolute bleakness can flatten emotional contrast unless purposefully intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern Fables
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror functions as cautionary tales conveying lessons about truth, consequence, and societal critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use horror to explore moral or societal anxieties—craft stories that illuminate consequences or truths rather than only shocking for shock's sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Fiction's Power
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity sustains horror's intense assault effectively; longer works struggle maintaining constant intensity without relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor short forms when aiming for relentless intensity; longer narratives need pacing, relief, and escalation arcs to avoid desensitizing readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Monsters Needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional monsters (vampires, zombies) remain relevant but new creatures reflecting current fears deserve exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update or invent monsters that embody contemporary anxieties; reinventations should feel necessary and thematically connected rather than derivative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, Don't Tell Fear
rubrics_metrics.description: Never explicitly tell readers to feel scared; instead, create atmospheric conditions allowing fear to emerge naturally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid instructing emotions. Build scenes, sensory detail, and implication so readers infer and feel dread on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken Flashlight Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial illumination, wavering light, and incomplete information heighten dread more effectively than clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use limited perspective and fragmentary information to maintain suspense. Over-clarification often reduces terror; let gaps and uncertainty work for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional Story Elements Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror requires strong characters, compelling ideas, solid writing, and coherent plotting alongside scary content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize scares over craft. Treat character, theme, prose, and plot with equal seriousness—scares are amplified by strong storytelling foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Horror
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must engage authentically with their own fears. 'Write about what scares you,' as honest terror resonates most powerfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on genuine personal anxieties for authenticity. Forced or faux fears ring hollow; personal engagement creates resonance and specificity.
